source.title: Deep Learning in current Neuroimaging: a multivariate approach with power and type I error control but arguable generalization ability
source.authors: C. Jim'enez-Mesa; J. Ramírez; J. Suckling; J. Vöglein; Johannes Levin; J. Górriz; A. Adni; D. I. D. (dian)

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests natural-label generalization and performance after label permutation in neuroimaging datasets, extending the question to AE-SVM classifiers and a different data setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy for original and permuted labels, including training and test scores for cross-validation. Cited findings about other studies and values used only to choose configurations are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The paper measures classification by a linear SVM on 20-dimensional autoencoder features. The autoencoder learns input reconstruction, not the original or permuted class labels. These results therefore do not test V1's coexistence of supervised neural-network memorization and generalization. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that their implemented models generally lack sufficient effective capacity to fit corrupted labels as accurately as original labels. They report smaller training–test discrepancies for the more complex configuration and for two-condition versus one-condition designs. They recommend upper-bounded resubstitution for statistical studies because of its computational cost, statistical power and false-positive control. Their suggestion that changing validation methods mitigates generalization error is an interpretation, not a demonstrated improvement in held-out predictive performance.
record.recipe_differences: AE feature extraction followed by a linear SVM; neuroimaging datasets and label-permutation evaluation, with 10-fold CV or upper-bounded resubstitution.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-test separation varied by dataset and design: the authors describe larger separation in one-condition designs than in two-condition designs.

fits_no_version.finding: The AE–linear-SVM pipelines have original-label CV test accuracies of 0.8319, 0.8458, 0.4396 and 0.6286. Their permuted-label training accuracies are 0.4791, 0.6455, 0.4066 and 0.6260, with permuted-label test accuracy near the corresponding chance levels. The DIAN original-label CV permutation comparison is not significant (p=0.0819).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low-dimensional autoencoder features followed by linear SVM classification can discriminate some neuroimaging labels while showing limited random-label fitting; this does not establish coexistence of neural-network memorization capacity and generalization.

record.problems: The study uses small neuroimaging datasets and an AE-SVM pipeline rather than the architectures in the named versions. Permuted-label training accuracy was not near-perfect, and the authors state that effective capacity to fit corrupted data was generally insufficient. Results vary by dataset and validation method.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for upper-bounded resubstitution, resubstitution, and control-subset/type-I-error experiments were omitted to prioritize the original-versus-permuted-label training and held-out CV accuracy comparisons relevant to V1; Tables 2–8 and 9–10 report these additional results.

untested.parts: Whether the same supervised neural architectures and training recipes can fit fixed random labels nearly perfectly while generalizing on natural labels. The neural component here instead minimizes reconstruction MSE, with batch normalization and restricted training budgets.
No width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No matched convolutional versus fully connected comparison on the same image task; architecture differences are confounded with datasets.
Adam is used without comparison against SGD or other optimizers.
No comparison of batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout intervention or corresponding held-out performance comparison.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization gaps.
No influence-based identification and removal of memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical accuracies match the cited tables. Permuted-label CV results use 100 repetitions, yielding 1000 fold-level values; original-label results use 20 repetitions. Additional validation methods and control-subset experiments are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows. Neither reduced random-label fitting by this constrained hybrid pipeline nor chance random-label test performance warrants a verdict against V1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the named CIFAR-10 architectures or ImageNet/Inception V3. Uses AE feature extraction with a linear SVM on neuroimaging datasets, rather than the named architectures and recipes.
